To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

molecular genetic analyses have enormous potential for improving the systematic status of marine organisms, but that the results of these studies are highly variable across groups, and are often difficult to interpret.

molecular genetic analyses are a powerful tool to resolve the systematic relationships among marine species, and that the results of these analyses can be applied in many different ways to address a wide array of ecological and evolutionary questions.

Molecular genetic analyses of species in marine microbes, invertebrates, and vertebrates show that: (1) morphologically similar species are frequently genetically distinct; (2) genetically distinct species are often morphologically indistinguishable; (3) hybridization occurs in many groups; and (4) species boundaries in some groups are older than 3 Myr, but in others they may be younger.

the genetic and evolutionary basis for species boundaries, and the application of these findings to the conservation and management of biodiversity.
